episodes.title: Crypto’s Biggest Heist Ever + The Spy Who Loved Nvidia + Hacktober’s Unsolved Mysteries
episodes.about: North Korea stole $6 billion from Binance in about 20 minutes, according to the FBI, making it the biggest crypto heist ever. Roose and Newton break down how the attackers got in, why investigators think the laundering may have been automated, how Binance covered the losses, and whether AI played a role. Then New York Times reporter Ana Swanson joins on Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive U.S. officials believe was a Chinese spy who got close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and the loophole that lets Chinese companies rent banned Nvidia chips. Plus the unsolved Hacktober cases: who took down AO3, the internet's biggest fanfic archive, and who hacked supermarket freezers across Europe and cranked them to 122 degrees.
episodes.why: The Nvidia segment carries the AI stakes: a suspected spy close to Jensen Huang, a White House that was briefed and did not act, and a rental loophole for banned chips - wrapped around a $6 billion heist the FBI says took 20 minutes.

episodes.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
episodes.about: The Democratic wave is bringing new scrutiny to AI, but how much will actually change? NLW breaks down the election's implications for data center construction, AI regulation, and the emerging 2028 presidential race - and why the backlash could lead to a better deal for local communities rather than a halt to the AI build-out.
episodes.why: NLW separates what a Democratic Congress can actually change - data center permits, AI regulation, 2028 positioning - from what stays the same, and makes the case the backlash ends in better terms for host communities, not a stopped build-out.

episodes.title: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
episodes.about: Nilay's guest is Willy Shih, an economist and professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, author of the upcoming book Where Does My Stuff Come From? They get into the economics underneath the AI boom: Trump's tariffs, the RAM price hikes and global memory shortage squeezing hardware, and why China remains a global manufacturing powerhouse even though every other country treats that as a risk.
episodes.why: Out today: Shih prices the part of the AI boom you can hold - every data center is chips, memory, and components crossing borders, and tariffs plus the memory shortage are quietly taxing each build.

episodes.title: ChatGPT for Teens' safeguards don't work, risk assessment finds
episodes.about: OpenAI's new teen-appropriate version of ChatGPT may not be living up to its promises, according to an independent evaluation. The new mode is supposed to have stronger guardrails for sensitive topics, automatic parental alerts, and a study tool that won't just give kids the answers to their homework. But the nonprofit Common Sense Media evaluated the tool and found it poses 'unacceptable risks.' Tom Siegel, who leads the Youth Safety Institute at Common Sense and tested about 4,000 prompts using fake teen accounts, speaks with Meghan McCarty Carino about his findings.
episodes.why: A test, not a take: Common Sense ran about 4,000 prompts through ChatGPT's teen mode using fake teen accounts and still found risks it calls unacceptable - in seven minutes, with the tester himself explaining where the guardrails failed.

episodes.title: Demis Hassabis says society is “not ready” for the AI future
episodes.about: Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis says the world is not ready yet for what's next in AI. He joins Reid Hoffman to talk about how to effectively govern frontier AI and why a more diverse group of experts needs a seat at the table. The conversation was recorded live at the Masters of Scale Summit in October 2026 at the Presidio Theatre in San Francisco.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Masters of Scale is Reid Hoffman's interview show, new here: Hassabis, recorded live at its summit, lays out how he would govern frontier AI and who he thinks is missing from the table making those calls.
